en.title: Netflix Secures The Walking Dead Universe for $500 Million Deal
en.summary: The entire Walking Dead saga, spanning over 350 episodes, is now officially a Netflix staple in a massive global licensing agreement. This deal solidifies the streamer as the definitive home for all things zombie apocalypse.
en.body:
Get ready to dive back into the zombie-infested world, because **The Walking Dead Universe** is officially making a more permanent home on Netflix. In a colossal global licensing deal reportedly worth over $500 million, Netflix has secured the streaming rights to the original **The Walking Dead** series and all of its major spin-offs.

This landmark agreement means that over 350 individual episodes of the franchise, from its gritty beginnings to its most recent expansions, will be available on Netflix through 2032 in numerous territories, including the UK, Italy, Australia, and New Zealand. For years, **The Walking Dead** and its offshoots have been a consistent performer for AMC, proving to be one of the network's most enduring and popular franchises. This deal elevates its status, making Netflix the undisputed destination for fans worldwide, whether they're newcomers eager to binge the entire saga or longtime survivors looking to revisit their favorite moments.

## A New Era for Zombie Fans

Netflix has had a varied history with the zombie genre, experiencing both hits and misses with its original content like **Black Summer** and **All of Us Are Dead**, alongside licensed titles. However, the sheer scale of this **Walking Dead Universe** acquisition underscores the franchise's immense value and proven track record. It’s a clear indication that the streamer sees the zombie apocalypse as a reliable engine for sustained viewership, especially among its core demographic of passionate, mobile-first fans who crave serialized storytelling.

This move also strategically positions Netflix to capitalize on the franchise's continued expansion. With multiple spin-offs already exploring new characters and corners of the apocalypse, this deal ensures that all future narrative threads will be readily accessible on a single, dominant platform, fostering a more unified fan experience and potentially encouraging deeper engagement with the sprawling universe created by **Robert Kirkman**.

## What This Means for the Fandom

For the dedicated fanbase, this comprehensive Netflix deal is a game-changer. It eliminates fragmentation, allowing for seamless marathon viewing sessions without jumping between platforms or waiting for regional availability. The sheer volume of content – over 350 episodes – represents a significant commitment from both Netflix and AMC, signaling that the universe is far from over and will continue to be a priority for years to come. This consolidation is likely to further solidify the community's shared experience, making discussions and theories even more accessible as new series and seasons are released.

## What's Next

While specific details on the rollout of all series across all territories are still being finalized, the immediate implication is that fans can expect a vast library of **The Walking Dead** content to become available or remain accessible on Netflix. Future spin-offs and potential revivals will almost certainly follow this streaming model, cementing Netflix as the ultimate command center for the zombie apocalypse.

content_raw: Every single project in The Walking Dead Universe is headed to Netflix in a licensing deal worth in excess of $500 million, accounting for over 350 individual episodes. Here’s your complete guide to every spinoff in the series.  Netflix has dipped in and out of the zombie business over the years with varied success. The streamer has had its disappointing entries, such as Resident Evil (2022). But then, there have been acclaimed hits like Black Summer, Kingdom , and perhaps most of all, Korean drama All of Us Are Dead . Outside of Netflix’s original offerings, they have also picked up plenty of zombie titles; in fact, only recently, Netflix licensed zombie series Revival from Syfy . Beyond that, some of the most acclaimed zombie franchises out there are Netflix — most significantly, The Walking Dead .  The Walking Dead Universe has a storied history on Netflix. Over the years, it has proven to be one of the streamer’s most enduring licensed titles from AMC. The franchise, based on the comics of the same name by Robert Kirkman, is a behemoth of television, and was the biggest show on cable for several years running. Across the main show and all of its spinoffs, there are over 350 individual episodes, and the franchise is showing little signs of ending. This summer, Netflix and AMC struck a gigantic $500 million global agreement , seeing the original series and its major spin-offs streaming on Netflix through 2032. That includes expansion to major territories, such as UK, Italy, Australia, and New Zealand. All of that is to say, Netflix is the one-stop home for the future of The Walking Dead .  Whether you’re new to The Walking Dead or you’re an old fan looking to re-kindle your interest in the franchise, choosing an avenue to watch it can be hard. Of course, the main series is the obvious (and best) starting point. But beyond that, the spinoffs weave in and out of each other, and sometimes only make sense if you’ve seen adjacent episodes, and so on. Down below, we’ve compiled our complete guide to every spinoff coming to Netflix. Plus, the franchise overseer Scott Gimple has offered a deeper insight into what’s in store for the future of The Walking Dead . Let’s take a tour.  The Walking Dead Seasons 1 (2010) – 11 (2022) Core cast: Andrew Lincoln (Rick Grimes), Danai Gurira (Michonne), Norman Reedus (Daryl Dixon), Steven Yeun (Glenn Rhee), Melissa McBride (Carol Peletier), Lauren Cohan (Maggie Rhee), Chandler Riggs (Carl Grimes), Jeffrey Dean Morgan (Negan) The Walking Dead is the mother show of the franchise and the glue that ties all of the spinoffs together. The series begins with Rick Grimes (Lincoln) waking up in a hospital in Atlanta. Alone and wounded, he soon realises that the hospital is empty and abandoned, but for the undead that lurk in its halls.
